items.title: A Review of Digital Strategies for Strengthening Public Service Delivery Systems
items.abstract: Digital transformation is now central to strengthening public service delivery, yet evidence on how digital strategies collectively improve public sector performance remains fragmented. This study presents a systematic review of digital strategies for enhancing public service delivery systems, with a primary focus on the United States and supporting international insights. Drawing on peer-reviewed literature published since 2015, the review examines e-government platforms, artificial intelligence, smart government technologies, open data initiatives, and broader digital transformation approaches. A thematic narrative synthesis is used to assess implementation practices, outcomes, and contextual conditions shaping effectiveness across levels of government. The findings show that digital strategies can significantly improve efficiency, transparency, accountability, and citizen engagement when they are citizen-centered, strategically aligned, and supported by strong data governance and organizational capacity. Digitalization expands service accessibility, streamlines administrative processes, strengthens evidence-based decision-making, and enables participatory governance. However, these gains are uneven and constrained by persistent challenges, including digital exclusion, organizational resistance, cybersecurity and privacy risks, limited resources, and weak interoperability. Successful initiatives integrate technology with change management, workforce development, cross-agency coordination, and adaptive governance. This review synthesizes fragmented evidence into a coherent framework that informs inclusive, secure, and sustainable digital transformation in public service delivery.

items.title: A Scoping review of “Nursing-Techonology Collaboration” in Home-Based Rehabilitation for the Elderly Under the Long-Term Care Insurance System
items.abstract: 1. Research Background and Research Questions The global aging population is accelerating, and the prevalence of chronic comorbidities, physical functional decline, and cognitive impairment has led to a continuous increase in the demand for home-based care among the elderly. By 2025, the long-term care insurance system had covered 190 million people, with expenditures exceeding 85 billion yuan. Home-based rehabilitation has become a priority service model under the long-term care insurance system due to its advantages, including aligning with the elderly’s preference for aging in place, reducing the costs of institutional care, and maintaining family and social connections. However, the implementation of home-based rehabilitation faces severe human resource constraints—a persistent global shortage of care workers persists. Meanwhile, older adults often suffer from multiple coexisting chronic conditions, polypharmacy, cognitive impairments, and fall risks, placing higher demands on caregivers’ professional skills and the frequency of care services. Against this backdrop, relying solely on human care is no longer sufficient to meet these needs, creating an urgent need to introduce technological solutions to address the labor shortage. In recent years, the rapid development of emerging technologies—such as digital health technologies, artificial intelligence, the Internet of Things, and social assistive robots—has provided entirely new solutions for home-based rehabilitation. However, whether technology can truly improve the outcomes of home-based rehabilitation hinges on the collaborative working model between caregivers and technological systems—that is, “caregiver-technology collaboration.” Currently, systematic research on “caregiver-technology collaboration” remains fragmented, lacking a comprehensive analysis of its classification, influencing mechanisms, and implementation pathways. 2. Research Objectives This scoping review aims to systematically review existing research on “nurse-technology collaboration” in home-based rehabilitation for the elderly under the long-term care insurance system. Specific objectives include: Describing the main types of “nurse-technology collaboration” models currently in use (e.g., triadic collaboration among nurses, physicians, and patients; robot-caregiver collaboration; closed-loop systems involving passive monitoring and caregiver response); To analyze the division of tasks, information flow, and decision-making mechanisms between nursing staff and technology in each collaboration model; To identify key factors influencing the effectiveness of “nursing-technology collaboration” (e.g., technology reliability, user acceptance, ethics and privacy, institutional support); To highlight the limitations of existing research and suggest directions for future studies. 3. Methods This study will follow the scoping review methodological framework proposed by Arksey and O’Malley and will be reported in accordance with the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Specific steps include: Search strategy: A systematic search will be conducted in Chinese and English databases, including PubMed, Web of Science, CINAHL, Scopus, and CNKI, covering the period from the inception of each database to April 2026; Inclusion Criteria: Include original studies, reviews, and theoretical articles in Chinese and English that explicitly discuss collaboration models between nursing staff and technicians within the context of long-term care insurance systems or home care; Data Extraction and Analysis: Use thematic analysis to extract key information from the literature, including types of collaboration models, task division, information-sharing mechanisms, decision-making mechanisms, and influencing factors, followed by classification, induction, and comprehensive analysis. 4. Expected Outcomes Map the research landscape of “nurse-therapist collaboration” in home-based rehabilitation for the elderly under the long-term care insurance system; Propose a classification framework for “nurse-therapist collaboration” models; Identify knowledge gaps to provide references for subsequent empirical research and service policies. 5. Research Significance This review is the first scoping review to focus on “nursing-technology collaboration” models within the context of the long-term care insurance system. Its innovations lie in: first, integrating the institutional context (long-term care insurance) with technological collaboration; and second, systematically summarizing the collaborative mechanisms between nursing staff and technology in home-based rehabilitation. The research findings can provide a theoretical basis for the integration of technology into home-based rehabilitation services and serve as a reference for service innovation and the optimization of payment policies within the long-term care insurance system.

items.title: A Unified Topological and Tensor Framework for Interpretable AI in Networks, Fraud, and Power Systems
items.abstract: Abstract: This study investigates whether a common mathematical representation can support accurate and interpretable artificial intelligence across cyber-network monitoring, transaction fraud detection, and power-system analytics. A unified framework is proposed in which domain observations are mapped to simplicial or graph-derived topological objects, embedded into third-order tensors, and processed through interpretable learning operators that preserve local structure, temporal dependence, and cross-scale interactions. The framework is designed to address a persistent limitation in applied AI: high-performing models often remain difficult to audit when deployed in safety-critical or economically sensitive environments. By combining persistent topological summaries with tensor factorisation and attribution constraints, the framework seeks to improve both predictive fidelity and explanation stability. Empirical evaluation is organised around realistic public benchmark settings: network intrusion records derived from KDD Cup 1999, highly imbalanced European card transaction fraud records, and real household electricity consumption observations used as a proxy for operational power-system load behaviour. Performance is assessed with accuracy, F1 score, ROC-AUC, precision-recall behaviour, calibration error, and explanation consistency. Across the three domains, the unified model yields stronger balanced performance than conventional tabular baselines and demonstrates particular advantages under class imbalance and regime shifts. The results indicate that topological descriptors improve robustness to structural irregularities, while tensor representations preserve multi-way relationships that are otherwise diluted in flattened feature spaces. The findings support a broader methodological argument: interpretable AI in complex infrastructures benefits from representations that respect shape, connectivity, and temporal composition rather than treating all observations as independent vectors. The proposed framework does not eliminate domain-specific modelling requirements, but it provides a coherent backbone through which anomaly propagation, fraud concentration, and load instability can be analysed within the same formal language. This creates a credible basis for future research on transparent AI architectures in networked and energy-intensive systems. items.title: Adapting and validating an artificial intelligence literacy scale for Ethiopian higher education using structural equation modeling
items.abstract: This study adapts and validates the Artificial Intelligence Literacy Scale (AILS) for higher education faculty in Ethiopia. After expert review and a pilot test with 40 participants identified four items with weak factor loadings, the research team revised those items to improve clarity and contextual relevance. The final 12-item English version was administered to 376 faculty members from four public universities. Exploratory factor analysis using principal axis factoring with oblique rotation confirmed a four-factor structure—Awareness, Usage, Evaluation, and Ethics—that explained 72.89% of the total variance. Confirmatory factor analysis showed good model fit (CFI = 0.977; TLI = 0.969; RMSEA = 0.061; SRMR = 0.049). Reliability and validity tests produced strong results: Cronbach’s α ranged from 0.856 to 0.930, composite reliability (CR) from 0.856 to 0.930, and average variance extracted (AVE) from 0.665 to 0.816. Multi-group confirmatory factor analysis supported configural, metric, and scalar invariance across both data collection methods (online and paper-based) and gender, confirming stable measurement properties. The adapted AILS provides a reliable, concise, and contextually sensitive tool for measuring AI literacy among faculty in low-resource higher education environments. The study highlights implications for curriculum design, faculty professional development, and cross-cultural adaptation of AI literacy assessments.

items.title: ADOPTION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE-DRIVEN LIBRARY SERVICES IN ACADEMIC LIBRARIES IN SOUTH-SOUTH NIGERIA
items.abstract: The study investigated the extent of Artificial Intelligence (AI) adoption in academic libraries in South-South Nigeria. It identified the types of AI tools currently in use, examined librarians' perceived benefits of AI-driven services, and the challenges constraining effective and strategic AI deployment in academic library environments. A mixed-methods research design was employed. Quantitative data were collected using a Four-Point Likert-Modified Rating Scale questionnaire administered to 100 professional librarians across six federal universities in South-South Nigeria. Qualitative data were obtained via semi-structured interviews with 12 ICT/system librarians. Descriptive statistics were used to analyze the data collected, while thematic analysis was used for the interview to complement and deepen quantitative findings. Findings revealed a low overall level of AI adoption (38.9%) in the studied academic libraries. Among available AI applications, plagiarism detection tools recorded relatively high usage, whereas advanced tools such as chatbots, predictive analytics, voice-based interfaces, and facial recognition technologies were minimally deployed. Respondents nonetheless reported high perceived benefits of AI adoption, including faster information access, improved user engagement, enhanced cataloguing accuracy, and stronger decision-support capabilities. Major challenges identified included inadequate ICT infrastructure, insufficient funding, shortage of skilled personnel, weak institutional AI policies, and technophobia among library staff. Qualitative evidence further showed that library services remain largely manual, with AI use being situational rather than strategically planned. The study concludes that despite strong perceived value and positive attitudes toward AI among librarians, effective adoption in academic libraries in South-South Nigeria remains limited by structural, financial, and capacityrelated constraints. To advance AI-driven library service transformation, the study recommends sustained investment in digital infrastructure, targeted human capital development, formulation of clear institutional AI implementation policies, and the establishment of sustainable funding mechanisms. These findings provide evidence-based guidance for innovation planning, technology investment, and digital readiness strategies in Nigerian academic libraries and comparable developing-country contexts.

items.title: Advanced Voice-Driven AI Frameworks For En-terprise Incident Analysis And Escalation Workflows
items.abstract: The increasing complexity of enterprise infrastructures, cloud computing environments, and distributed operational systems has created major challenges in incident management, escalation handling, and real-time operational support. Traditional support engineering methods often de-pend on manual monitoring and reactive troubleshooting approaches, which can result in delayed incident resolution, operational downtime, and reduced service reliability. Recent advancements in Artificial Intelligence (AI), Natural Language Processing (NLP), speech recognition, machine learning, and generative AI technologies have enabled the development of advanced voice-driven AI frameworks that support intelligent enterprise operations and automated escalation workflows. This research paper explores advanced voice-driven AI frameworks for enterprise incident analy-sis and escalation workflow management by integrating voice-enabled AI assistants, predictive analytics, intelligent automation, and machine learning models to improve operational monitoring, incident classification, troubleshooting assistance, and escalation coordination. The study empha-sizes the importance of Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) methodologies in which human experts supervise AI-generated recommendations and validate critical escalation decisions to ensure relia-bility, transparency, accountability, and operational accuracy. Voice-driven AI assistants allow support engineers and operations teams to interact with enterprise systems through natural lan-guage commands, thereby improving accessibility, reducing response time, and enhancing collab-orative decision-making during critical operational incidents. The paper further examines the applications of voice-driven AI systems in enterprise operations centers, cloud infrastructure management, cybersecurity incident response, and intelligent IT service management. The pro-posed framework provides several benefits including faster incident resolution, proactive anomaly detection, improved operational efficiency, optimized resource utilization, reduced downtime, and enhanced customer satisfaction. Additionally, the research discusses key challenges such as data privacy concerns, speech recognition accuracy, AI explainability, integration complexity, and cybersecurity risks associated with intelligent operational systems. Finally, the study highlights future research directions in adaptive AI systems, explainable voice interfaces, generative AI support agents, and autonomous enterprise operations, demonstrating how advanced voice-driven AI technologies can transform enterprise incident analysis and escalation workflows through the effective combination of intelligent automation and expert human oversight.

items.title: Advanced Voice-Driven AI Frameworks For En-terprise Incident Analysis And Escalation Workflows
items.abstract: The increasing complexity of enterprise infrastructures, cloud computing environments, and distributed operational systems has created major challenges in incident management, escalation handling, and real-time operational support. Traditional support engineering methods often de-pend on manual monitoring and reactive troubleshooting approaches, which can result in delayed incident resolution, operational downtime, and reduced service reliability. Recent advancements in Artificial Intelligence (AI), Natural Language Processing (NLP), speech recognition, machine learning, and generative AI technologies have enabled the development of advanced voice-driven AI frameworks that support intelligent enterprise operations and automated escalation workflows. This research paper explores advanced voice-driven AI frameworks for enterprise incident analy-sis and escalation workflow management by integrating voice-enabled AI assistants, predictive analytics, intelligent automation, and machine learning models to improve operational monitoring, incident classification, troubleshooting assistance, and escalation coordination. The study empha-sizes the importance of Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) methodologies in which human experts supervise AI-generated recommendations and validate critical escalation decisions to ensure relia-bility, transparency, accountability, and operational accuracy. Voice-driven AI assistants allow support engineers and operations teams to interact with enterprise systems through natural lan-guage commands, thereby improving accessibility, reducing response time, and enhancing collab-orative decision-making during critical operational incidents. The paper further examines the applications of voice-driven AI systems in enterprise operations centers, cloud infrastructure management, cybersecurity incident response, and intelligent IT service management. The pro-posed framework provides several benefits including faster incident resolution, proactive anomaly detection, improved operational efficiency, optimized resource utilization, reduced downtime, and enhanced customer satisfaction. Additionally, the research discusses key challenges such as data privacy concerns, speech recognition accuracy, AI explainability, integration complexity, and cybersecurity risks associated with intelligent operational systems. Finally, the study highlights future research directions in adaptive AI systems, explainable voice interfaces, generative AI support agents, and autonomous enterprise operations, demonstrating how advanced voice-driven AI technologies can transform enterprise incident analysis and escalation workflows through the effective combination of intelligent automation and expert human oversight.

items.title: Advancing target discovery through disease-specific integration of multi-modal target identification models and comprehensive benchmarking system
items.abstract: Target identification is crucial for drug development. AI-driven approaches leveraging multi-omics and computational modeling can accelerate this process. However, integrating multi-modal data for disease-specific target identification and predicting translational potential remains challenging. Moreover, the absence of a systematic evaluation framework for model performance limits confidence in target reliability. This study presents a unified framework combining machine learning-based target identification with comprehensive benchmarking. We first developed Target Identification Pro (TargetPro), a disease-specific model spanning 38 diseases across oncology, metabolic, immune, fibrotic, and neurological categories. TargetPro shows strong predictive performance for clinical-stage targets and reveals disease-specific patterns, underscoring the need for tailored target detection models. We next created Target Identification Benchmark (TargetBench 1.0) to assess target identification systems, including large language models, based on their ability to recover established targets and find high-quality novel candidates. This integrated approach offers a streamlined strategy to evaluate target discovery models, ultimately improving drug development efficiency.

items.title: AI and the Soul of Medicine
items.abstract: The rapid integration of large language models into clinical medicine raises ethical, philosophical, and existential questions that extend beyond traditional concerns about patient safety and data privacy. These artificial intelligence systems now perform clinical tasks such as diagnostic reasoning, protocol selection, and patient communication at levels comparable to trained physicians, yet the frameworks governing their deployment remain anchored in an era when machines could not convincingly simulate human understanding. The ethical implications of incorporating large language models into healthcare are examined through the lens of historical precedent, the physician-patient relationship, and the evolving meaning of human agency in clinical care. Drawing on examples from organ transplantation, intensive care medicine, and genetic engineering, medicine has repeatedly absorbed technologies that challenged foundational ethical assumptions, and each such absorption required the development of new governance frameworks rather than the rejection of the technology itself. Three critical tensions specific to large language models emerge: the gap between linguistic competence and genuine understanding, the redistribution of clinical authority from physicians to algorithms, and the erosion of empathy as a uniquely human contribution to healing. Ethical integration of large language models into medicine requires not only the application of existing bioethical principles but also the development of new frameworks that address the unprecedented capacity of these systems to inhabit the communicative and relational spaces previously reserved for human clinicians.

items.title: AI Based Career Recommendation System
items.abstract: Choosing the right career path is one of the most critical decisions in a student’s life, yet many students face confusion due to lack of proper guidance and awareness of their skills and interests. The AI-Based Career Recommendation System is designed to assist students in identifying suitable career options based on their academic performance, skills, interests, and aptitude. The proposed system reduces dependency on manual counseling, minimizes bias, and provides accurate and data-driven career guidance. By leveraging artificial intelligence, the system helps students make informed decisions about their future careers and understand the skills required to achieve their goals. This project demonstrates the effective use of AI and ML in real world decision-support systems.

The Data Science platform is the start and more subjects will be added to make it even better.

items.title: AI Deepfake audio detection using CNNs (Real Talk)
items.abstract: With the rapid advancement of Generative AI, voice cloning has emerged as a significant threat, often used as a primary tool for financial scams and misinformation. My work, titled "Real Talk," details the development of an AI-driven system designed to distinguish between authentic human speech and fabricated vocal patterns. The system utilizes Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to classify audio data by analyzing digital discrepancies. Leveraging signal processing techniques such as MFCC extraction and spectrogram visualization via Librosa, the model was trained on industry-standard datasets, including ASVspoof and LibriSpeech. Technical implementation was performed using Python with the TensorFlow, Keras, and PyTorch frameworks. Key features of the application include multi-format support (.wav, .mp3, .m4a), real-time processing, and a percentage-based confidence meter for authenticity reporting. Experimental results demonstrate a detection rate of over 85% with an analysis latency of less than 10 seconds, providing an accessible and efficient solution for non-technical users to verify audio integrity. This work was conducted at Arab International University (AIU), Syria. The official website of the university is: https://www.aiu.edu.sy
